If \(u\) and \(v\) are both functions of \(x\) then
\[\int u dv = uv - \int v du.\]

Let \(u = {{CT:2}}\) and \(dv = {{CT:3}} d{{CT:1}}\).

Then \(du = {{CT:4}} d{{CT:1}}\) and \(v = {{CT:5}}\).

So,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
\int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int u dv \\&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  uv - \int v du \\&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:2}}{{CT:5}} - \int {{CT:5}}{{CT:4}}d{{CT:1}} +c
 \end{array}\]

Hence,
\[2\int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}} = {{CT:6}}\]

And so,

\[\int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}} = \frac{{CT:7}}{2}+ \frac{c}{2}.\]
